fix: replace sexy mode escalation with exponential decay

The escalation algorithm had a hardcoded cap at 20 slaps, causing it
to alternate between only the last two audio files for the rest of the
session. This meant ~40 of the 60 files were never played, despite the
README advertising "60 levels of escalation."

Replace the fixed 5-minute sliding window + linear ratio mapping with
exponential decay scoring and an asymptotic 1-exp(-x) curve:

- Each slap adds 1 to a score that continuously decays (30s half-life)
- The score maps to file index via 1-exp(-(score-1)/scale), which
  asymptotically approaches but never reaches the last file
- Scale is auto-derived from the half-life, cooldown, and file count
- Intensity now reflects current slap *rate*, not just accumulated count
- Slowing down naturally lowers the level; stopping resets to baseline
- Zero per-slap allocations (replaces the []time.Time sliding window)

Merge pull request #3 from taigrr/cd/fix-event-detection-after-cap

fix: detect new events after detector trims event buffer

fix: detect new events after detector trims event buffer

The detector caps Events at 500 entries, trimming old ones from the
front. The previous check (len > prevCount) would fail once the slice
was trimmed, since the length could stay the same or decrease. This
caused spank to stop detecting slaps after ~500 events.

Switch to tracking lastEventIdx and using != instead of > to correctly
detect new events regardless of internal trimming.

Closes #2

feat: initial release — slap your MacBook, it yells back

Detects physical impacts on Apple Silicon MacBooks via accelerometer
(reads from sensord shared memory). Two modes:
- Pain mode: random 'ow!' responses from 10 clips
- Sexy mode (--sexy): escalating responses based on slap frequency

Uses embedded MP3 audio via go:embed, gopxl/beep for playback,
and apple-silicon-accelerometer for vibration detection.
